topics.title: EU budget talks pause
topics.summary: European Union leaders ended a long budget negotiation without agreement, leaving a proposed Ukraine loan in limbo while they plan another attempt in three weeks.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a group cannot agree after a marathon meeting, is a pause a sign of failure or the sensible way to make room for better ideas?

topics.title: New Zealand election balance
topics.summary: New Zealand's governing coalition fell one seat short of a parliamentary majority, leaving a centrist party with potential influence over the next steps.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you enjoy being the small group everyone needs to win an argument, or would that much attention make you want to hide?

topics.title: New tariff questions
topics.summary: The United States announced tariffs affecting a range of countries, prompting businesses and governments to weigh what changing trade rules could mean for prices and supply chains.
topics.discussionPrompt: When trade rules change, which everyday item would you notice first getting pricier: food, clothes, electronics, or cars?

topics.title: A panda's first birthday
topics.summary: Rio, described as Indonesia's first homegrown giant panda, celebrated a first birthday as the country marked the young animal's milestone.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you had to plan a birthday for an animal ambassador, what would make the best gift: a giant snack, a new climbing setup, or a very quiet day?

topics.title: Frozen water under pressure
topics.summary: A new study highlighted growing strain on Earth's frozen-water systems, drawing attention to changes affecting glaciers, snow, sea ice and communities that rely on them.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which kind of ice landscape feels most magical to you: a snowy forest, a frozen lake, sea ice, or a distant glacier?

topics.title: Wild neighbours at home
topics.summary: A study reported that roughly 2,000 wild species live alongside people in homes, a reminder that domestic spaces can host far more nature than we notice.
topics.discussionPrompt: What is the most surprising non-pet creature you have shared a home with, and was it a welcome guest or an accidental roommate?

topics.title: Yukon power project advances
topics.summary: A Yukon power-infrastructure proposal has moved to Canada's Major Projects Office, putting a northern energy project into a new federal review process.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your town could upgrade one piece of shared infrastructure, would you choose cleaner power, transit, internet, or something else?

topics.title: Asteroid-crater closeups
topics.summary: New images of asteroid Dimorphos are helping researchers examine the aftermath of NASA's earlier impact test and refine ideas for planetary-defence planning.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you rather watch a space mission from mission control, a backyard telescope, or a live stream with friends and snacks?

topics.title: Learning a new language
topics.summary: BBC science programming explored what research can say about learning a second language, revisiting a familiar challenge for curious learners everywhere.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could become conversational in one language overnight, which would you pick, and what is the first thing you would want to say?

topics.title: AI data centres in space
topics.summary: A Guardian report examined the idea of putting AI data centres in space, looking at the technical ambitions and practical questions behind the proposal.
topics.discussionPrompt: If computing moved into orbit, what would amaze you most: the engineering, the view, or the challenge of keeping everything cool?
